findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy: none; pct: 100

findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud against customers and fleet partners, increasing fraud and insurability risk; enforcement is a low-cost pre-close remediation item.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none through quarantine to reject after validating SPF/DKIM alignment and rua reporting.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier: ~all; lookup_count: 2

findings.deal_impact: Softfail weakens spoofing protection and compounds the DMARC p=none issue, sustaining impersonation risk for invoices and payment instructions.

remediation.summary: Validate authorized senders, then change SPF ~all to -all in coordination with DMARC enforcement.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.deal_impact: Unsigned DNS increases cache-poisoning/redirection risk for web and mail, though impact is lower than the email-auth and exposed-appliance findings.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC signing at the registrar/DNS provider and publish DS records, with key-rollover procedures.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems
findings.deal_impact: Publicly logged vpn, jenkins-old, staging-api and legacy-portal names suggest an attack surface that may include weakly managed legacy/staging access; requires ownership validation in diligence.

remediation.summary: Inventory the 4 risky hostnames, remove or restrict legacy/staging/admin systems, and confirm VPN patching and MFA.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size
findings.deal_impact: 47 unique hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests possible asset sprawl and incomplete inventory, complicating patching and incident response.

remediation.summary: Reconcile all 47 CT hostnames to owners and business purpose; decommission orphaned hosts and certificates.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support: TLSv1.0: true, TLSv1.1: true, TLSv1.2: true; tls_versions: [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www may fail customer/compliance expectations and weaken transport protection, especially alongside the VPN appliance exposure.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 on www, retain TLSv1.2+ with modern ciphers, and verify client compatibility.

findings.title: HSTS not set
findings.deal_impact: Without HSTS on both hosts, users are more exposed to downgrade/MITM attacks; a quick hardening win with limited deal materiality alone.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security on apex and www after confirming HTTPS-only operation for all subdomains.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001; vendor: ExampleGate; product: ExampleGate SSL-VPN; matched_fingerprint version: 7.0.11, kind: appliance, host: www.brightwaterfleet.example; match_tier: appliance_exposed; note: KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure of an internet-facing ExampleGate SSL-VPN to a known-exploited product listing (version not verified) could enable initial access; validate patch level urgently pre-close.

remediation.summary: Verify ExampleGate SSL-VPN 7.0.11 against the KEV CVE, patch/upgrade or isolate the appliance, enforce MFA, and review VPN logs for compromise.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: type: state_ag_breach_notice; date: 2025-08-14; summary: Notice filed for unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified.; entity_match: exact; disclosed_within_months: 14

findings.deal_impact: A state AG breach notice 14 months ago involving ~3,100 individuals signals prior customer-support compromise, potential notification/regulatory tail, and insurance disclosure relevance.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident report, root-cause and remediation evidence, regulatory closure status, and cyber-insurance history for the 2025-08-14 notice.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.deal_impact: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts lacked MFA enforcement, indicating privileged production access was not consistently protected and was exposed through a legacy provisioning bypass.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: **Exception noted.** 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.deal_impact: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days versus a 1-business-day requirement, creating prolonged unauthorized-access risk after employment ended.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: **Exception noted.** 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in security monitoring (CC7.2)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.deal_impact: Security alerts were unreviewed for two consecutive weeks, creating a monitoring blind spot during which incidents could have gone undetected or untriaged.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: **Exception noted.** For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in change management (CC8.1)

evidence.excerpt: **Exception noted.** 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.deal_impact: 2 of 40 sampled production changes lacked documented peer approval, weakening change-control assurance for emergency deployments.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: **Exception noted.** 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided
findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.1 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, bypassing conditional access via a legacy provisioning script.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.2 exception: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, not same-day revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC7.2 exception: for 2 consecutive weeks in Nov 2025, alerts went to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC record is p=none with policy none, so DMARC is monitoring-only, not enforced; spoofing is not blocked.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: State AG breach notice on 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access to a customer support system, with approximately 3,100 individuals notified.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT log presence alone does not prove a host is live, but legacy-portal (last_seen 2026-07-22) and jenkins-old (2026-08-14) had certificates within the last 12 months, showing active maintenance contradicting prior decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: Annual penetration test control had no exceptions, but 2 high-severity findings were reported, contradicting 'clean, no highs'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 control A1.2-01 was tested with no exceptions: production data is backed up daily to immutable storage and restore tests are performed quarterly.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: No bridge letter was provided; E-030 is only an unaudited management plan to obtain one upon request, which is not positive evidence corroborating the claim.

deal_recommendations.text: Make signing conditional on verification and a compromise assessment for the internet-facing ExampleGate SSL-VPN exposure during Days 0–30, with a bring-down of security representations at signing.

Commission a scope covering the known-exploited-product exposure and independent validation of management representations, sequenced with the Days 0–30 work, to satisfy full cyber diligence required before signing [F-008].
Seek a specific indemnity for pre-closing incident losses tied to the disclosed incident, informed by the Days 31–60 incident review and full cyber diligence required before signing [F-009].

Proceed on the basis that the known incident is likely excluded from representations and warranties coverage, resolve any gap before close after the Days 31–60 review, and reflect full cyber diligence required before signing [F-009].

Confirm insurability and likely underwriting requirements before close, using remediation of email spoofing and privileged-access controls in Days 31–60, within full cyber diligence required before signing [F-001] [F-010] [F-011].

Impose a post-close covenant to complete the remaining remediation across Days 31–60 and Days 61–100, sequenced after full cyber diligence required before signing [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-013] [F-001] [F-002] [F-004] [F-006] [F-009] [F-014].

Do not seek a price adjustment on cyber grounds alone because total remediation of $142K–$643K is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band, but preserve full cyber diligence required before signing and the windows from Days 0–30 through After day 100 [F-008] [F-009].

narrative.executive_summary: Bottom line: Escalate: full cyber diligence required before signing; Brightwater Fleet Systems, Inc. is rated D at 56.8 because of a critical, potentially exploitable exposure [F-008], a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months [F-009], and multiple management statements contradicted by evidence [C-001] [C-005]. Key risks: The internet-facing ExampleGate SSL-VPN is matched to a known-exploited-product listing with version not verified [F-008]. The 2025-08-14 incident involved approximately 3,100 individuals [F-009], privileged-access exceptions affected 4 of 25 admin accounts and 3 of 15 terminated users [F-010] [F-011], alerts were unreviewed for two consecutive weeks [F-012], and DMARC is not enforced [F-001]. Management credibility: Of 9 claims assessed, 7 were contradicted, 1 was unsupported, and 1 was supported, spanning MFA, offboarding, alert review, DMARC, incident history, legacy systems, and penetration-test results [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005] [C-006] [C-007]. Next steps: Complete full cyber diligence before signing, verify and compromise-assess the VPN in Days 0–30 [F-008], and obtain the incident report and regulatory status in Days 31–60 [F-009].
key_questions_for_management: Provide evidence of the ExampleGate SSL-VPN version, patch status, MFA enforcement, and VPN log review, and confirm whether compromise assessment has been completed [F-008].

Provide the incident report, root-cause analysis, remediation evidence, regulatory closure status, and cyber-insurance history for the 2025-08-14 breach notice involving approximately 3,100 individuals [F-009] [C-005].
Reconcile the statement that every admin account is behind MFA with the exception affecting 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts, and provide current MFA enforcement evidence [F-010] [C-001].
Reconcile same-day automated offboarding with 3 of 15 terminated users retaining access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, and provide current termination-access records [F-011] [C-002].
Provide the alert-routing and review records covering Nov 10–23, 2025, and confirm the current distribution and escalation process [F-012] [C-003].
Provide the plan and validation evidence for moving DMARC from p=none to enforcement and changing SPF from ~all to -all [F-001] [F-002] [C-004].
Provide an inventory reconciling all 47 hostnames, including the 4 risky hostnames, to owners and business purposes and confirm which legacy or staging systems remain active [F-004] [F-005] [C-006].
Provide a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30 and the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report for the carved-out infrastructure hosting service [F-014] [F-015] [C-009].

exceptions.description: **Exception noted.** 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.
exceptions.management_response: Management disabled the legacy provisioning script in April 2026 and has begun migrating service-desk accounts to the standard conditional access policy. Migration expected to complete Q3 2026.

exceptions.description: **Exception noted.** 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.
exceptions.management_response: Management is evaluating an automated HR-to-IdP de-provisioning integration. Until then, terminations are processed manually by IT upon email notification from HR.

exceptions.description: **Exception noted.** For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.
exceptions.management_response: The distribution list was corrected on November 24, 2025. Management has added a weekly check that alert routing is functioning.

exceptions.description: **Exception noted.** 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).
exceptions.management_response: Management has updated the emergency change procedure to require post-deployment approval within 48 hours.
